fact: The MFWA report, as relayed by The Nation, cites the suspension of international broadcasters in Burkina Faso (with Mali and Niger) over alleged bias; no date or outlet named, and the report spans six years, so as_of is the document's published date.

The Centre national de presse Norbert Zongo's digital-rights report says that in 2024 the suspension of certain international media continued to cover their online access, and the online platforms of RFI, France 24, Jeune Afrique and Le Monde, among others, remained inaccessible in Burkina Faso; the document does not name the ordering body or an end date.

fact: CIVICUS Monitor reports the General Student Union of Burkina Faso (UGEB) issued a statement criticising the government's security record and the military authorities' failure to restore security.

CIVICUS Monitor reports the Minister of Territorial Administration suspended UGEB for three months on 26 May 2026 after its statement, and the Ouagadougou prosecutor opened an investigation into its authors.
CIVICUS Monitor reports the Higher Council for Communication indefinitely suspended TV5 Monde broadcasts on 5 May 2026 (decision 2026-018/CSC) over its coverage of terrorism and Mali.

Human Rights Watch says Burkina Faso's media regulator ordered the suspension of broadcaster TV5Monde on 5 May 2026, accusing it of 'disinformation' and 'apology of terrorism' over its reporting on armed groups.
